plan.alert_summary:
Incident window is about 17:28–18:03 on 2025-12-15, in namespace otel-demo. Several alerts look like background noise because they fire from the start and are unrelated to the app. These are Watchdog, KubeSchedulerDown, KubeControllerManagerDown, PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers, KubeClientCertificateExpiration and InfoInhibitor.

The alerts that matter appear in this order:
- 17:37 RequestErrorRate (warning) on frontend-proxy, the earliest app-level signal.
- 17:53 CPUThrottlingHigh (info) on the postgresql pod in otel-demo, at 33% throttling.
- 17:54 RequestErrorRate on frontend.
- 17:55 RequestErrorRate on cart.
- 17:56 KubePodCrashLooping on valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft, with CrashLoopBackOffPodsDetected (critical) at 17:56:48.
- 17:57 RequestLatency above 1500ms on frontend-proxy, frontend and cart.
- 17:58 RequestErrorRate on checkout.
- 18:02 RequestLatency on checkout.

The likely story is that valkey-cart, the cart's datastore, started crash-looping. That would push errors and latency from cart up through frontend and frontend-proxy, then to checkout. This is only a hypothesis. The frontend-proxy errors began at 17:37, about 20 minutes before the valkey crashloop, so they may have a separate or earlier cause. Chaos-mesh objects exist in the cluster, so a chaos experiment is possible.

Trace spans only cover 17:20–17:33, which is before most of the alerts. Logs, metrics and k8s events cover the full window. Use traces for the dependency graph and early baseline, and rely on metrics and logs for the later period.

assignments.focus: Find what changed before or around 17:37, when frontend-proxy errors started, and before 17:56, when the valkey-cart crashloop began. Check for chaos-mesh experiments, rollouts or config changes in otel-demo, and for OOMKills, restarts and scaling. Look at valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft (restart reasons, exit codes, limits), the postgresql pod and flagd. Say which change is the earliest and which is the most likely trigger.

Look at error and warning logs in otel-demo from 17:28 to 18:01. Start with valkey-cart (why it crashes: OOM, a bad config or a failed connection), then cart, frontend, frontend-proxy and checkout. Find the first error message for each service and whether cart errors mention valkey or redis connection failures. Also look for what explains the frontend-proxy errors at 17:37.

Build a timeline of anomalies from 17:28 to 18:03 for valkey-cart (memory, CPU, restarts), the postgresql pod (CPU throttling) and the pods behind frontend-proxy, frontend, cart and checkout (error rate, latency, CPU, memory). Decide whether the valkey-cart memory or CPU issue came before the cart errors, and what changed at about 17:37.

Spans only exist from 17:20 to 17:33, so use them as a baseline and for the dependency graph. Map the calls among frontend-proxy, frontend, cart, checkout and the flagd and valkey dependencies. Look for error spans or latency, and for any feature-flag-related failures, in the early window. Say which downstream service is most likely the root cause of the frontend-proxy errors.

finding.summary: Traces (only 17:20:40–17:33:07) show no request-path failures. Trace error rate is 0% for frontend-proxy, frontend, cart, checkout and product-catalog, and p95 latencies are normal (frontend-proxy 526 ms, frontend 208 ms, cart 96 ms, checkout 367 ms). The only errors are a handful of flagd EventStream streaming-RPC errors (fraud-detection, ad, recommendation, flagd) between 17:20 and 17:32. These are feature-flag stream timeouts, not request failures, and their volume is tiny (about 6 error spans out of roughly 1,800 flagd spans). Traces contain no spans for valkey-cart, and the window closes before the 17:37 frontend-proxy alert, so traces cannot confirm or rule out the valkey-cart crashloop hypothesis or identify the cause of the frontend-proxy errors. The dependency graph is: load-generator→frontend-proxy→frontend→{product-catalog, cart, ad, recommendation, checkout}; checkout→{currency, cart, shipping, product-catalog, payment, email}; and flagd is called by load-generator, cart, ad, recommendation and fraud-detection. Trace data does not support naming a downstream root cause for the frontend-proxy errors. Metrics, logs and k8s events need to cover 17:28–18:03 to check valkey-cart, the postgresql CPU throttling, and any chaos-mesh experiment.

Together these make valkey-cart the most likely trigger for the 17:56 crashloop, with the stress schedule as a possible contributor. The 17:37 frontend-proxy errors have no matching change in the change or event data; the data-recorders namespace created at 17:37:47 came after the alert. I could not retrieve restart reasons or exit codes (no OOMKilled event or termination state surfaced), so the OOM link is inferred from the limit, not confirmed. Also, I could not retrieve the chaos-mesh Schedule or StressChaos objects by name; their status comes from events only.

finding.summary: Logs show valkey-cart is the earliest failure point in the app-level chain, but my signal cannot show why it crashes. valkey-cart has no log lines at all in the window, so OOM, bad config and crash messages are not visible. The first failure in the dependent chain is cart losing its Redis connection at 17:53:08, about 3 minutes before the 17:56:48 CrashLoopBackOff alert. Cart's Redis failures continue until at least 18:01:29. Cart's own logs say "Connection failed" and "Wasn't able to connect to redis", which points at valkey/redis connectivity. Frontend and checkout have no error log lines of their own. Their errors show up only as 504 timeouts at frontend-proxy, starting at 17:54 for /api/cart and 17:56 for /api/checkout. The 17:37 frontend-proxy alert is only weakly supported: the logs show sporadic 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started errors starting at 17:36:05, with one at 17:37:23 on /api/recommendations. No matching error appears in recommendation or flagd logs, and I found no cause in logs for these. Chaos-mesh is outside my signal and I did not verify it.

finding.summary: Metrics do not show a discrete change at 17:37. Several series drift upward from the start of the window (17:29), so the 17:37 frontend-proxy alert is not explained by a step change in any metric I could read. Among the valkey-cart signals, CPU throttling is the one that accelerates before the cart errors. Memory stays flat. The valkey-cart CPU throttled-periods counter (cumulative) rises slowly from 17:29 (163 → 383 by 17:51) and then steepens sharply: 383 at 17:51, 461 at 17:53, 649 at 17:55, 670 at 17:57, 762 at 17:59, 832 at 18:01. Cart error rate starts at ~0 at 17:53, reaches 8.75 at 17:55 and 36 at 17:57. The valkey working set stays at ~2.2–2.6 MB average through 17:51, with only brief spikes to ~7 MB (17:51, 17:59) and no sustained climb, so memory exhaustion is not supported. The crashloop (17:56) and the drop in valkey samples at ~18:01 come after the cart errors had already started. Working conclusion: valkey-cart CPU saturation/throttling (starting ~17:51) came before the cart errors (17:53) and the crashloop (17:56). Postgresql CPU throttling counter also rises steadily from 17:29 with no step at 17:37, so it looks like a gradual load effect, not a trigger. Caveats: the frontend-proxy error_rate series I queried returned values (~467) that do not match the alert value (1.43), so I did not use it. Cart duration_p95 rises gradually from 1.5 s (17:29) to 4.1 s (17:50) and then ~11 s (17:52+), so latency builds before the 17:57 alert. Trace data and the k8s events/logs (which would show the 17:37 change and the valkey restart reason) are outside my metric scope. I did not find a chaos experiment in metrics.

contributing_factors.name: chaos-mesh/Schedule/otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress
contributing_factors.reasoning: The chaos-mesh memory-stress schedule that targets valkey-cart is the earliest in-cluster change. It has been spawning StressChaos experiments since 17:29:37, before any app alert. The valkey-cart container has a 10Mi memory limit, so the stress most plausibly starves valkey-cart. That would cause its CrashLoopBackOff at 17:54–17:56. Cart then loses its Redis connection, so cart returns errors and timeouts. Those propagate to frontend and frontend-proxy as 504s, and then to checkout. The valkey-cart pod and the cart, frontend, frontend-proxy and checkout services are downstream effects of the stress. The postgresql CPU throttling is a gradual load effect and is not a separate cause.
contributing_factors.evidence: Schedule events: reason=Forbid, 40 events from 17:29:37 to 18:01:13 ('Forbid spawning new job because: otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress-4fvng is still running'). Child StressChaos objects show 'Failed to apply chaos: no running task found'. valkey-cart limits are memory=10Mi and cpu=10m, with an unchanged spec. BackOff events 17:54:04–18:01:22. KubePodCrashLooping fired at 17:56:40 and CrashLoopBackOffPodsDetected at 17:56:48. Cart logs show 'Connection failed' from 17:53:08 and 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' from 17:54:11. Frontend-proxy 504s on /api/cart from 17:54 and on /api/checkout from 17:56. RequestErrorRate and RequestLatency alerts fired on cart, frontend, frontend-proxy and checkout. Caveats: the OOMKilled reason was not confirmed, and the Schedule and StressChaos objects could not be retrieved, so their status comes from events only. The 17:37 frontend-proxy error alert has no identified cause.

verdicts.reasoning: This is the only fault-injection object aimed at valkey-cart. It has been spawning StressChaos runs against valkey-cart since 17:29:37, before any app alert. One run was applied to the earlier valkey-cart pod (dj5q5) at 17:32:11. The valkey-cart container has a 10Mi memory limit, so memory stress is a plausible trigger for the CrashLoopBackOff and the cart, frontend and checkout errors that follow. Caveats: most runs logged 'no running task found', and no OOMKilled reason or exit code was available. The causal link is therefore inferred and not proven. fix_plan.summary: The likely root cause is the chaos-mesh Schedule `otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress`. It repeatedly runs memory StressChaos against valkey-cart, which has a 10Mi memory limit. valkey-cart then crash-loops, and cart, frontend and checkout fail with it. I checked the cluster state. The valkey-cart Deployment is unchanged at revision 1, with no spec change in the window, so a rollback would do nothing. The only recorded change to it is its Endpoints object, which follows the pod restarts. The diagnosis itself says the chaos link is inferred, not proven. None of the five allowed actions touches a chaos-mesh Schedule or StressChaos object. A restart or scale would only treat the symptom, because the next stress run would crash the pod again. I'm proposing no actions.
fix_plan.escalate: A person with chaos-mesh access should pause or delete the Schedule `chaos-mesh/otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress`. For example, they could set `spec.suspend: true` or run `kubectl -n chaos-mesh delete schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress`. They should also delete any active StressChaos runs against valkey-cart, such as `psc57`. Once the stress has stopped, valkey-cart should recover on its own as the CrashLoopBackOff backoff expires. If it does not, restart the valkey-cart Deployment. Next, they should confirm the cause. Check the last terminated state of pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft for OOMKilled and its exit code. Then check that cart's "Wasn't able to connect to redis" errors stop. If crashes continue with no chaos running, review the 10Mi memory limit in the Helm values. That limit is very tight for valkey, and changing it is outside the allowed actions.
